item.question: When preparing a dataset for modelling, you notice that some columns have a large proportion of their values missing, while other columns are missing values only occasionally across many rows. Compare the two main strategies for handling missing values and explain the circumstances under which each is the better choice.
item.answer: Two approaches are described. (1) Removal: dropping rows or columns that have missing values, commonly those exceeding a certain threshold. This is suitable when the rows or columns being removed contain many missing values, so removing them does not discard important information from the modelling process. However, when missing values occur only sparsely across many rows or columns, removal trims much needed information from the dataset. (2) Imputation: filling in missing values with a specific value; a typical simple method is to impute using the mean, median or mode of a variable, and more recent research suggests using advanced techniques such as multiple imputations or interpolation. Each approach has its own advantages and disadvantages.
